email.scenario: You study English every day with a language-learning app called WordTrail, and you have enjoyed its short daily lessons for several months. After the app updated itself last weekend, all of your saved vocabulary lists and your study record disappeared. You have a placement test next week and were relying on those lists to review.
email.subject: Vocabulary lists missing after the latest update
bullets: Tell the support team what you appreciate about the app's daily lessons.
Explain what happened to your vocabulary lists and study record after the update.
Ask the team to restore your lists from a backup before your placement test next week.

academicDiscussion.professorPost: This week we are looking at how community arts events decide who performs. Many small towns hold an annual music festival, and organizers must choose who gets the main stage. Some give it to local amateur performers, while others book well-known visiting acts and place local musicians on smaller side stages. What do you think? Should a town music festival fill its main stage with local amateur performers rather than well-known visiting acts? Why or why not?

studentPosts.name: Mirela
studentPosts.post: I think the main stage should belong to local amateurs. A town festival exists for the town, and playing for a large audience is how new performers improve and get noticed. Famous bands already have plenty of stages. If locals are always pushed to a side tent, they never get the experience that helps them grow.

studentPosts.name: Tobias
studentPosts.post: I disagree. Without a famous name on the poster, far fewer people buy tickets, and the festival loses the income that pays for sound equipment, security, and everything else. A well-known visiting act brings a big crowd, and local musicians who play earlier that day reach more listeners than they ever would alone.
